thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Reverse Linked List”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input head = [1,2,3,4,5] should still produce [5,4,3,2,1].

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(n).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To reverse a singly linked list, we need to reverse the direction of the pointers while traversing the list. We maintain three pointers: 'prev' (to keep track of the previous node), 'current' (to keep track of the current node), and 'next_node' (to keep track of the next node in the original list). In each iteration, we update the 'current.next' pointer to point to the 'prev' node, and then move 'prev' and 'current' pointers one step forward. We repeat this process until we reach the end of the original list, and the 'prev' pointer will be pointing to the new head of the reversed list.

solutions.python:
# Reverse Linked List
# Idea: To reverse a singly linked list, we need to reverse the direction of the pointers while traversing the list. We maintain three pointers: 'prev' (to keep track of the previous node), 'current' (to keep track of the curren…
# Line comments below keep the same logic as the NeetCode 150 repo solution.

# Definition for singly-linked list.
# class ListNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.next = next


class Solution:
    def reverseList(self, head: ListNode) -> ListNode:
        prev = None
        current = head

        while current:
            next_node = current.next
            current.next = prev
            prev = current
            current = next_node

        return prev
